title: For Whom the Bell Tolls
author: Ernest Hemingway
current_text: In Spain, censors prohibited publication of For Whom the Bell Tolls until 1968, when a censored Spanish translation was published under the title Por quién doblan las campanas.

sources.quote: The original English edition was published as early as 1940, but it was not until 1968 that the novel was finally published in Spain in a translated – and censored – version under the title Por quién doblan las campanas. This article deals with the publication, translation, and censorship history of said novel in Francoist Spain.
sources.title: Literarische Zensur im Franquismus: Rezeption und Zensur von Ernest Hemingways For Whom the Bell Tolls (1940) | apropos [Perspektiven auf die Romania]

sources.quote: Los censores prohibieron la publicación de la novela Por quién doblan las campana s hasta el año 1968.
sources.title: LA CENSURA FRANQUISTA DE HEMINGWAY EN ESPAÑA | Matadero Madrid

ban_rows.note: In 1973, the book was banned in Turkey because it included 'propaganda unfavorable to the state.'
Banned by military junta for its portrayal of the Spanish Civil War and anti-fascist themes.
